goal: Deliver STACKFALL v1.0: an original, offline, deterministic 2D tetromino block-stacking game for the Anbernic RG503 handheld (ROCKNIX/PortMaster), written in C++17 with an SDL2 platform layer and a pure headless rules core, procedural graphics drawn only from rectangles/lines and a 5x7 glyph table, synthesized sound, persistent high scores, complete automated rule and regression tests, a native AArch64 binary with a PortMaster launcher and package, and release acceptance on the physical device at about 60 FPS.

tasks.title: Create CMake project with core, game, and test targets
tasks.details: Round M0. Create the repository layout from the specification: README.md, LICENSE, docs/SPEC.md, include/stackfall/, src/, tests/, portmaster/. CMake with Ninja exposes three targets: stackfall_core (portable static library, no SDL2 linkage), stackfall (links stackfall_core and SDL2), stackfall_tests (links stackfall_core only, so rule tests run headless). Acceptance: cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug and cmake --build build complete without errors, and ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure runs the initial test suite with no window.

tasks.title: Desktop SDL2 window, controller detection, fixed 60 Hz loop
tasks.details: Round M0. Implement src/main.cpp: SDL2 window and renderer on the 960x544 logical canvas, SDL GameController discovery with keyboard fallback, clean EXIT shutdown, and a fixed-step accumulator based on SDL_GetPerformanceCounter/Frequency with dt = 1/60 s. Poll events as often as possible, run the required number of simulation ticks, render once, clamp the elapsed frame delta to 250 ms after resume or suspend, and log unusual stalls. Acceptance (M0 gate): compiles cleanly on desktop; the test executable runs without a window; the blank window opens, logs any detected controller, and exits cleanly.

tasks.title: Define types and the seven tetromino shape tables
tasks.details: Round M1, kickoff step 1. Add include/stackfall/types.hpp (board constants W=10, H=20, HIDDEN=2; PieceId; Rotation states 0/R/2/L; cell helpers) and pieces definitions for I, O, T, S, Z, J, L with the canonical spawn drawings. Spawn centered at matrix originX=3, so I spans columns 3..6 and O spans 4..5, with the topmost occupied cell at y=-1: I uses originY=-2 (first occupied local row 1), all others use originY=-1. Acceptance: tests prove each of the seven pieces has exactly four occupied cells in each of its four orientations (specification section 11, item 1).

tasks.title: Implement SRS rotation with wall-kick tables
tasks.details: Round M1, kickoff step 2. Add immutable precomputed orientation masks and canonical ordered kick tables for 0<->R, R<->2, 2<->L, L<->0. JLSTZ share one table, I has its own, O stays stationary. Negate the reference +y kick values when encoding them, because grid +y points down; keep one convention in code and tests (reference: tetris.wiki/SRS). Try up to five candidate offsets and take the first valid one, or reject the rotation and leave the piece unchanged. Acceptance: tests prove O never moves or kicks; I and JLSTZ orientations match known SRS reference cases; rotation against walls applies a valid kick or fails without moving; rotation above the hidden-row boundary never reads or writes outside y=-2..19 (section 11, items 2, 3, 5, 6).

tasks.title: Implement bitmask board, collision, lock, line clears
tasks.details: Round M1, kickoff step 3. Implement the board: std::array<uint16_t,22> occupancy using bits 0..9 (a full row is 0x03FF) plus a parallel 22x10 cellType array for block colors. Validate moves against the ten columns, y=-2..19, and settled occupancy bits. Commit the four active cells on lock, then remove all full rows simultaneously and shift remaining rows down, moving occupancy and color rows together. Assert the two arrays stay consistent in tests and debug builds. Acceptance: tests prove settled cells block movement, the active piece is not committed before lock, 1/2/3/4-line clears remove the correct rows with colors shifting, and randomized fills keep occupancy and colors consistent over hundreds of cases (section 11, items 7, 8, 17).

tasks.title: Implement PCG32 randomizer and seven-bag queue
tasks.details: Round M1, kickoff step 4. Implement an explicitly coded PCG32 generator seeded once per game, a Fisher-Yates shuffle of the seven piece IDs, consumption of the whole bag before the next shuffle, and a queue filled far enough ahead to always show the next five pieces. Use no platform-dependent C++ distribution code in the deterministic core. Acceptance: tests prove every seven-draw bag is a permutation of I/O/T/S/Z/J/L and fixed seeds reproduce fixture sequences exactly (section 11, item 13).

tasks.title: Implement game state machine and deterministic tick
tasks.details: Round M1, kickoff step 5. Implement Game::start(seed) and Game::tick(const InputFrame&) on a single thread with no SDL types. Cover: the level 1-20 gravity table (48 ticks per cell down to 1); soft drop of one cell per held tick with +1 point per successful cell; hard drop to the lowest valid y with instant lock and +2 points per cell; 30-tick grounded lock delay with at most 15 resets per active piece (failed inputs never reset it); DAS of 10 ticks and ARR of 2 ticks; movement stops at walls in every orientation; hold once per locked piece with spawn rotation/position reset; block-out on failed spawn and lock-out when locked cells sit in hidden rows; clear scoring 100/300/500/800 multiplied by the pre-clear level; level = min(20, 1 + floor(totalLines/10)); pause freezing all counters; and the input processing order from section 5. Keep gameplay RNG separate from any cosmetic randomness. Acceptance (M1 gate): headless tests pass for gravity timing, pause and restart, lock delay and the reset limit, hard-drop landing in the same tick, drop-point accounting, hold restrictions, top-out determinism, and score/level boundaries including the level 20 cap (section 11, items 4, 9, 10, 11, 12, 14, 15, 16).

tasks.title: Add state-hash regression runner with pinned values
tasks.details: Round M1, kickoff step 6. Implement the regression test: compute a stable game-state hash after a supplied replay of tick-indexed input frames, accept --seed <integer> on the developer test CLI for reproducibility, and pin hash values compared by ctest. Acceptance: identical seeds and identical tick input streams produce identical hashes and scores on repeated desktop runs (section 7; section 11, item 18 desktop half).

tasks.title: Build SDL input adapter for controller and keyboard
tasks.details:
Round M2. Translate SDL GameController events and desktop keyboard input into the core InputFrame, with one mapping table so controller letters change in a single place. Load SDL_GAMECONTROLLERCONFIG from the PortMaster environment when present. Follow the section 5 table: D-pad move and soft drop, A rotate clockwise, B rotate counter-clockwise, X hard drop, Y or left shoulder hold, Start pause; keyboard Left/Right/Down, X/Up and Z rotate, Space hard drop, C/Left Shift hold, Enter/Esc pause. Edge-trigger rotation, hold, hard drop, pause, and menu actions; use the tick-based DAS/ARR repeat for horizontal movement; simultaneous left+right causes no movement, and a newly pressed opposite direction resets DAS/ARR and moves immediately when valid. Process SDL events before simulation. Acceptance: tests or recorded desktop sessions prove a press edge is consumed exactly once even when the loop catches up over several ticks (section 11, item 19), and both keyboard and controller drive the game.

Unattended verification policy: Use automated SDL event injection and a virtual controller for desktop acceptance. Cover pending input across pause, restart, focus loss, and controller removal. Human input and physical controller testing are deferred to final acceptance. T023 provides the reusable driver.

tasks.title: Implement procedural renderer and 5x7 glyph font
tasks.details: Round M2. Implement a read-only Renderer::draw(const Game&) that never mutates game state. Use SDL_RenderSetLogicalSize or equivalent letterboxing for a 960x544 logical canvas. Draw 24x24 cells with the board at origin (360, 32) spanning 240x480, the hold panel around x=52..324 on the left, and the five next previews plus score, lines, and level around x=630..910 on the right. Follow the section 6.2 draw order: background, optional faint grid, board frame and settled cells in their stored colors, ghost below the active piece, active piece, hold and next previews (same shape coordinates at about 15 px cells), then score fields and menus. Render all text from a source-defined 5x7 integer bitmask glyph table using filled rectangles; use the seven-color custom palette. No texture or image loading calls anywhere. Acceptance: the desktop build renders board, ghost, hold, next previews, and text with no asset files present.

tasks.title: Complete title, controls, pause, and game-over screens
tasks.details:
Round M2. Implement the section 4.7 state machine: TITLE with Start Game, Controls, Quit, and the saved high score (0 until persistence lands in the M3 task); CONTROLS with the mappings and back; PLAYING; PAUSED overlay with Resume, Restart, and Quit to Title, with every counter frozen exactly; GAME_OVER with final score, total lines, level, new-record indication, Play Again, and Title. Restart begins a fresh seeded game; Quit to Title abandons the round. Menu navigation uses D-pad up/down with A to select and B to go back. Acceptance (M2 gate): a full game plays from title to game over using both keyboard and controller on desktop, with no external graphics.

Unattended verification policy: T024 verifies the first playable gate through the real SDL input path and inspected screenshots. Complete the implementation without waiting for a human desktop session or physical device.

tasks.title: Add atomic high-score persistence
tasks.details: Round M3. Implement storage: a small versioned UTF-8 ASCII file in the writable conf/ directory (example: version=1 on one line, high_score=12345 on the next), honoring the XDG_DATA_HOME or explicit save-directory environment variable set by the launcher. Write through a temporary file in the same directory, flush, close, then rename into place. Save when a new record is set at game over; on a missing, invalid, or partial file, recover safely to high score 0 without crashing. Acceptance: tests prove good records round-trip after relaunch and corrupt or partial files never crash the game (section 11, item 20).

tasks.details:

Log startup version and architecture, SDL init failures, the selected renderer and controller, any save failure, and orderly shutdown to log.txt. Acceptance: forced-failure runs (for example, with audio unavailable or a restricted video driver) show the documented fallback or a clean exit instead of a crash, and the log contains the required entries.

Unattended verification policy: Add a fallback frame limiter when presentation does not block, including software rendering. tasks.title: Profile and optimize performance in a bounded loop
tasks.details: Round M3. Execute docs/PERFORMANCE.md after T025 and before the T015 desktop gate. Build reproducible Release benchmarks from fixed seeds and real SDL scenarios. If the optional runner is unavailable, the executing agent performs the same loop without a human prerequisite.
